## TL;DR

Review pass 3 fixed the periodic completed-capture reaper so it can run while a shot is still tracked as live on the Mac. The reaper no longer waits for an idle host or zero active jobs, and it does not skip containers listed in `liveContainerNames` for the completed-capture path — remote removal still re-validates completion logs, quiet output, and idle CPU immediately before `docker rm -f`.

## Work and rationale

The incident pattern is a runner that logs `[browser-capture] runner browser capture completed`, writes `result.json`, then sits at ~0% CPU for many minutes because the Bun process never exits. The Mac blocks on container exit unless the result poll wins the race. Review passes 1–2 added explicit runner exit, Mac-side force-collection when `result.json` is stable, handoff cancellation, Hetzner parity, and a shared `runValidationContainerReaper` with a completed-capture branch.

Review pass 3 found a scheduling gap: the very container this task targets is excluded from the belt-and-braces reaper. Hetzner’s `maybeRunReaper` bailed out while `activeJobs > 0`, and Tailscale only scheduled the reaper when `effectiveActive(s) === 0`. Both providers also registered the in-flight capture container in `liveContainerNames`, and `runValidationContainerReaper` skipped those names for completed-capture candidates. So when the poll path failed or the Mac was still waiting, the periodic sweep could not remove the hung container that motivated #1060.

The fix separates concerns between validation stale sweeps and completed shot sweeps. Stale validation containers still honor `liveContainerNames` and the inspection path from #1049. Completed shot containers use an empty active-name filter when building candidates — age alone is enough to enter the list — and the per-container `completedCaptureReaperCommand` re-checks capture mode, completion log lines, two minutes of silence, and sub-1% CPU before removal. Scheduling no longer requires the host to look idle: Tailscale runs the shared reaper whenever a host is probed, healthy-enough, and not already reaping; Hetzner runs it on the same interval without gating on `activeJobs`.

Documentation in `docs/remote-validation.md` now states that the Mac-side sweep can run while a capture is still tracked as live, with the remote boundary checks called out explicitly.

## Approaches tried

Earlier rounds concentrated on the primary recovery path: polling for `result.json` during the SSH session and tearing down the named container on success. That addresses the common case when the control plane is actively collecting. The review correctly noted that acceptance criterion 3 (watchdog/reaper) was ineffective for the hung-but-tracked-as-live scenario because of scheduling and exclusion logic, not because the remote removal script was wrong.

An alternative was to remove a container from `liveContainerNames` as soon as the completion log appears remotely. That would unblock the stale candidate list without changing scheduler guards, but it risks the validation stale reaper treating a genuinely in-flight validation run as eligible unless we split sets per run kind. Running the completed sweep on busy hosts while keeping `liveContainerNames` for validation only avoids that ambiguity.

## Challenges and blockers

Balancing #1049’s “do not reap in-flight validation runs” with #1060’s “do reap completed hung shots” required two layers: scheduler permissiveness plus a stricter removal command for shots only. No live tailnet runner was exercised in this session; coverage is command-level shell tests and fake-exec integration tests, matching prior rounds.

## Key learnings

A hung shot container is often still “active” from the Mac’s perspective because collection has not finished. Safety for the completed-capture reaper belongs at the remote removal boundary (log + silence + CPU), not in the Mac-side live-name registry. The result.json poll remains the fast path; the periodic reaper is recovery when that path does not complete and the container orphan lingers.
